messages:
Maria H: quick question — for the routing policies editor, should we keep drag handles for reordering or switch to explicit rank inputs? :thinking:
Tony L: my vote: keep drag handles for quick reorders, but add a compact numeric affordance for precise positioning (esp. for long lists). keyboard focus needs love though.
Lee S: accessibility nit — if we keep drag handles we must provide a keyboard reorder mode and ARIA live announcements. right now screen reader just says 'list item' and nothing about its index.
Maria H: agreed re: ARIA. Can we show index labels (1., 2., 3.) that update live while dragging? would help both sighted and screen reader users.
Samir: +1 to index labels. Also we should show a small inline preview of the rule's result when you hover — like the sim sandbox but super lightweight. helps when priority ordering changes intent. :eyes:
Tony L: how heavy is the preview runtime? we can't call full sim for each hover. maybe render a cached sample output (static prompt + cached model run) and mark it as "example".
Samir: exactly — cached snapshots per rule. we already generate snapshots during evals. reuse those. UX just exposes them as a hover tooltip or a collapsible row.
DesignBot: Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/routing-editor-ordering — I added two variants: compact drag + index, and numeric-only.
Lee S: copy tweak: current validation says "Invalid rule" which is vague. propose: "Rule conflict: this rule will never match because a higher-priority rule covers the same condition." and then link to help. shorter on the line but explicit.
Maria H: love that. Also for inline validation states, prefer an orange warning for potential conflicts vs red for blocking errors. color contrast check needed.
Tony L: notes on interactions: when you drag a rule above another, preview pane should update in real-time to reflect new ordering (even if preview is cached). helps catch subtle priority regressions.
Samir: implementation detail: we can fake the reorder client-side and render preview from cached snapshots — no network roundtrip for the UI change.
Lee S: keyboard pattern proposal (for accessibility): select item, press Ctrl+Alt+ArrowUp/Down to move. announce: "Moved rule to position 2 of 8." Add a tooltip showing the shortcut.
Maria H: can we surface the "locked" state for system rules? they should be visually distinct and excluded from reorder (but still show where they fit).
Tony L: yes, show a lock icon and reduce opacity; keyboard move should skip locked entries. also show a tooltip: "System rule — cannot change priority."
Samir: on validation messages, add an action link: "Highlight conflicting rules" which expands the two involved rules in the canvas.
Maria H: PDP decision: aim to ship core interactions (drag + index label + cached inline preview + keyboard reorder + better validation copy) in next sprint. design handoff tomorrow morning.
Lee S: accessibility checklist for handoff: ARIA roles for listbox/listitem, live region announcements for position changes, keyboard shortcuts documented, color contrast numbers included, and descriptive alt text for icons.
DesignBot: handoff file: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/routing-editor-handoff — includes annotations and exported assets.
Tony L: dev question — what should the API call be for snapshot fetch? Samir: GET /api/v1/rules/:id/snapshot (cached) — returns preview text + model metadata. mark it as "sample_only" so we don't confuse it with live evals.
Maria H: small copy follow-up: change the preview label from "Sim result" to "Example outcome" — less technical for PMs.
Lee S: final check — make sure keyboard focus order is preserved when reordering (focus should remain on the moved item). otherwise screen reader users get lost.
Samir: noted. I'll put a small dev spike for focus management and simulated preview rendering.
Maria H: thanks team. I'll update the tickets: add acceptance criteria and link to the Figma handoff. landing PR target: end of sprint. :thumbsup:
Tony L: :thumbsup:
Lee S: :raised_hands:
DesignBot: +1 (automated: handoff created, id=HND-442)
